title: Gold prices near 1-year low, silver slides as dollar hits 19-month high: Should you buy before wedding season or wait? | Stock Market News
text:
Gold and silver prices showed signs of stabilisation on Tuesday, November 17, after suffering a sharp sell-off in the previous session. However, both precious metals remained close to their lowest levels in more than a year as a strengthening US dollar, elevated Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

Internationally, spot gold was little changed at $3,856.52 per ounce as of 0028 GMT on Tuesday, after touching its lowest level since October 2025 on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery edged up 0.2% to $3,859 per ounce, according to Reuters.

Silver gained 0.3% to $47.17 an ounce, recovering marginally after plunging 3.6% on Monday to its lowest closing level since October 2025.

The modest recovery follows a difficult week for bullion. Gold declined 4.5% last week, while silver also witnessed substantial selling pressure. High US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy have reduced the appeal of non-yielding precious metals.

The US dollar has emerged as a major headwind for precious metals, climbing to a fresh 19-month high against a basket of major currencies. The currency remained supported by stronger-than-expected US inflation data released last week and hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials.

A stronger dollar makes gold and silver, which are priced in the US currency, more expensive for overseas buyers, potentially weighing on demand.

Expectations of another interest rate increase by the US Federal Reserve have added to the pressure. According to the CME FedWatch tool, markets are pricing in a 96.6% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point increase stands at 3.4%, Reuters reported.

Higher interest rates and rising bond yields tend to reduce the attractiveness of gold and silver, as these assets do not generate interest income.

Investors are also monitoring developments in the US bond market, with the 10-year Treasury yield approaching 5.15%, according to Ashish Rajodiya, Head of Commodities at PL Capital.

Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said on Monday that emerging technologies could have a significant impact on the economy. He outlined scenarios ranging from stronger economic growth and broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and a possible slowdown if anticipated investment returns fail to materialise.

Market participants are now awaiting the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27–28 policy meeting, scheduled for release on Wednesday, 18 November, for further clues on the central bank's monetary policy outlook.

Domestic precious metals also witnessed significant selling pressure on Monday, 16 November, as the stronger dollar and elevated US Treasury yields weighed on sentiment.

Gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) closed around ₹1,34,550 per 10 grams, while silver settled at ₹1,68,001 per kg.

Both metals declined to multi-week lows amid concerns that the Federal Reserve could maintain a hawkish policy stance for longer.

Vikram Subburaj said gold and silver were attempting a modest recovery following last week's sharp sell-off, although the broader trend remained uncertain.

He noted that early electronic quotes on the MCX showed December gold trading at ₹1,36,750 per 10 grams, up ₹525 or 0.39%, while December silver futures gained ₹234 or 0.13% to ₹1,76,543 per kg. These early indications suggested some bargain-hunting, but the recovery remained limited.

Internationally, December COMEX gold futures rose 0.2% to $3,895.60 an ounce, while spot gold gained 0.3% to $3,892.42. Gold's 4.5% decline last week has made current levels attractive to some investors looking to rebuild positions, he said.

However, Subburaj cautioned that the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook remained a key influence on bullion prices. Higher interest rates and Treasury yields could continue to weigh on gold, while investors would also track oil prices and US inflation data for clues on the direction of monetary policy.

The October FOMC meeting minutes, due on Wednesday, could provide further guidance on the Fed's next policy move.

For Indian investors, movements in the rupee will remain important alongside international bullion prices. Silver could also experience larger price swings than gold because of its exposure to industrial demand.

Subburaj advised investors against chasing the initial recovery, recommending staggered buying and disciplined position sizing instead. He said the current rebound should be viewed as an attempt to stabilise rather than confirmation of a trend reversal.

Jateen Trivedi said gold continued to face selling pressure, declining by around ₹2,000 to ₹1,34,700 as dollar strength and rupee appreciation weighed on domestic prices.

He added that COMEX gold slipping below $3,875 had further weakened the technical outlook, with the next downside zone seen around $3,550–$3,600 in the coming weeks.

Overall sentiment remains weak, with market participants tracking Kevin Warsh's remarks and US retail sales data for further indications of the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory.

Trivedi expects domestic gold prices to remain volatile within the ₹1,32,000– ₹1,36,000 range in the near term. He advised investors to remain cautious given the continuing downside risks.

Ashish Rajodiya said gold and silver had fallen to their lowest levels in more than a year on Monday, with spot gold declining nearly 0.5% to around $3,863 an ounce and silver dropping approximately 3% to below $47.50.

On the MCX, gold traded below ₹1,35,900 per 10 grams, down nearly ₹1,000, while silver slipped below ₹1.71 lakh per kg, losing more than 3%.
